questions.q: Choose the most approitate word for blank 1?
questions.solution: Place strain on is the natural expression for overloading infrastructure. The surrounding sentence describes overcrowding.
questions.passage:
English Language
In the following passage, there are five blanks, each followed by a number corresponding to a question with five
options. Choose the option that fits each blank most appropriately.
Rapid urbanisation across the developing world has placed enormous (1)_____ on existing public transport
infrastructure. Cities that were designed decades ago for a fraction of their current population now (2)_____
with overcrowded buses, congested roads, and unreliable train services. Policymakers have responded with a
range of measures, from expanding metro networks to (3)_____ dedicated bus corridors that bypass traffic.
However, critics argue that such measures often (4)_____ the needs of low-income commuters, who are
frequently pushed to the periphery of new transit lines by rising property prices near stations. Unless urban
planning becomes more (5)_____, the very people who rely most heavily on public transport risk being left
behind by its expansion.

questions.q: Choose the most approitate word for blank 2?
questions.solution: Grapple with means struggle to manage a problem. It fits overcrowding and unreliable services.

questions.q: Her method of teaching mathematics was refreshingly _____, and she eventually turned her classroom anecdotes into a bestselling _____ that inspired thousands of readers.
questions.solution: Novel as an adjective means new or unusual. As a noun, it is a long fictional book.

questions.q: He needed someone to formally _____ his proposal so that it could be put to a vote, but he realised he had only a _____ to make his case before time ran out.
questions.solution: To second a proposal means formally support it. A second is also a short unit of time.

questions.q: After years of chasing promotions, she finally felt _____ with her current role, though her manager still worried about the _____ of her recent reports, which seemed rushed.
questions.solution: Content as an adjective means satisfied. As a noun, it means the substance contained in the reports.

questions.q: The (A) tiny startup, operating out of a garage with just three employees, secured a (B) modest seed investment of fifty thousand dollars, whereas the (C) multinational conglomerate, with offices in forty countries, raised a (D) staggering two billion dollars in its latest funding round.
questions.solution: The scale of each investment agrees with its business: a modest amount for the startup and a staggering amount for the multinational. No interchange is needed.

questions.q: Only after the (A) minor kitchen fire had barely singed the curtains did firefighters need (B) three hours and considerable effort to bring it under control, whereas the (C) massive wildfire that razed thousands of acres was put out (D) within seconds using a single bucket of water.
questions.solution: The small fire should be extinguished within seconds; the massive wildfire takes three hours and effort. Swap B and D.

questions.q: Neither the manager nor the employees was aware (A) / of the sudden policy change (B) / that had been implemented without (C) / any prior consultation. (D) / No error (E)
questions.solution: With neither…nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject employees. Replace was with were in part A.

questions.q: Hardly had the meeting begun (A) / when the fire alarm started ringing (B) / , forcing everyone to evacuate (C) / the building immediate. (D) / No error (E)
questions.solution: The verb phrase needs the adverb immediately, not the adjective immediate. The error is in D.

questions.q: The number of students who have applied (A) / for the scholarship this year (B) / are significantly higher (C) / than it was last year. (D) / No error (E)
questions.solution: The number is the singular head of the subject. Use is significantly higher, so C contains the error.

questions.q: She is one of those rare leaders (A) / who always listens to her team (B) / before making a final decision (C) / on any important matter. (D) / No error (E)
questions.solution: Who refers to the plural leaders in one of those leaders. Use who always listen in part B.
